claims.explanation: RITA binds p53 and disrupts the p53-MDM2 interaction, reactivating wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis. Selectivity is therefore expected for lines with wild-type TP53 and intact p53 pathway signaling; TP53 mutations or defects in downstream effectors (e.g., ATM, SF3B1) would confer resistance. The observed sensitive lines often have TP53 mutations, but these may be subclonal or not fully inactivating, and additional features like MDM2 amplification or high p53 target expression could further refine prediction.

features.basis: RITA requires wild-type p53 to induce apoptosis; TP53 mutations confer resistance.
High MDM2 may sensitize to RITA by disrupting p53-MDM2 interaction and freeing p53.
ATM loss impairs p53 activation and DNA damage response, reducing RITA efficacy.
SF3B1 mutations may disrupt splicing of p53 pathway components, conferring resistance.
CDKN2A loss may enhance apoptosis upon p53 reactivation by removing cell cycle arrest.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, which may cooperate with p53 to promote apoptosis.
BRAF mutations may sensitize to RITA via oncogene-induced stress and p53 dependence.
KRAS mutations may sensitize to RITA via oncogene-induced stress and p53 dependence.
EGFR mutations may sensitize to RITA via oncogene-induced stress and p53 dependence.
PIK3CA mutations may sensitize to RITA via oncogene-induced stress and p53 dependence.
RB1 loss may reduce apoptosis and confer resistance to p53-mediated cell death.
NF1 mutations may activate RAS/MAPK and alter p53 response, conferring resistance.
